main_body: Half-timbered house with a large hipped tile roof, a cream plaster front wall with a door and window, and a front gabled porch bay below
top_band: Roof slope: dark outline at row 2 (x=36) or row 0 (x=72), then brown tile rows (#804530 / #49252c stripes) down to about row 42. It reads as a big sloped surface seen from above, with a ridge and hips.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible sloped surface with a ridge, hip lines and an eave. Below it is a separate vertical half-timbered wall, with a dark eave row (rows 42-45) at the junction. The gabled porch bay at the front shows its own roof slopes above its front wall. Roof and wall are both clearly drawn, so it matches the Beodeul house pieces. The door and window are painted fairly flat, but they are small details. The main body passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours (references: 185 and 66) and a median of 3 colours per tile (references: 18 and 11). All of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a near-black sticker line; the references are 7% and 9%. The roof tiles are a two-tone stripe pattern with no per-tile highlights, and the wall is a flat cream fill with 17% flat-fill coverage. The references have 5-6 shading steps, scalloped tiles and stone and plaster texture. The candidate is much flatter and thinner than both.
